citation: Detrano, R., Janosi, A., Steinbrunn, W., Pfisterer, M., Schmid, J., Sandhu, S., Gopalakrishna, K., Belle, C., & Detre, K. (1989). International application of a new probability algorithm for the diagnosis of coronary artery disease. The American Journal of Cardiology, 64(5), 304-310.

target_binarisation.class_0_definition: Absence of coronary heart disease (<50% diameter narrowing in any major vessel)
target_binarisation.class_1_definition: Presence of coronary heart disease (>50% diameter narrowing in at least one major vessel)

missingness.handling_protocol: No global row dropping (no global dropna). Categorical missing cells are imputed with training-fold most frequent value via SimpleImputer within a scikit-learn Pipeline fit strictly on training folds.

preprocessing_protocol.continuous: Median imputation + StandardScaler, fit on train folds only
preprocessing_protocol.categorical: Most-frequent imputation + OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False), fit on train folds only
preprocessing_protocol.leakage_prevention: All transformations fit strictly inside cross-validation loops on training splits only.

limitations: Clinical tabular data collected at medical center; not time-series or wearable sensor telemetry.
Demographic skew toward older males (68% male).
intended_use: Benchmark evaluation for clinical tabular disease-risk classification baselines in academic research.
forbidden_use: Direct clinical diagnostic use, autonomous medical treatment decisions, or claiming physical sensor validation from tabular records.
